title: CSS Forge
description: Generate CSS custom properties, JSON, TypeScript and Style Dictionary tokens from a CSS Forge configuration, and keep the tokens of a design tool in sync with it.

sync.inbox.adopt.description: Adopt a token that the remote created: first add it to the configuration at a path of your choice, then record that path here. The next push renames the remote token to the name the configuration generates, and sets the value of the configuration, so designs that use the token keep it. Writes the state file only.

item.description: The id of the inbox item: the token name without its leading --.

path.description: The token path of the configuration token that the item becomes, added to the configuration before this call, e.g. palette.brand.accent. It is the path in the description of each pushed token (cssforge: <path>).

remote.description: The name of the remote, as `remote add --name` gave it.

root.description: The directory that the configuration path and the state directory .cssforge/sync resolve against. The default is the working directory.

sync.push.description: Read the remote, then send the changes of the plan: create and update the tokens of the configuration, delete the ones removed from it, and carry out the decisions on inbox items. Items without a decision stay in the inbox, and their tokens are not changed. One request to read, up to two to write and one to read the stored values back; only the first when the plan is empty.

sync.remote.add.description: Bind a file of a design tool to the configuration as a remote, so that the token sync commands read and write that file only. Checks that the remote can open the file (one request), and writes .cssforge/sync/<name>.json. Binding the same file again keeps the sync state; binding another file starts the sync again.

tokens.build.description: Generate the outputs of a CSS Forge configuration and write them to files: CSS custom properties, JSON, TypeScript and Style Dictionary tokens. Every output is generated before the first file is written, so an invalid configuration leaves the previous files in place. The result lists the files written and the warnings of the configuration.

tokens.built.description: Build the outputs of a CSS Forge configuration now, then again each time the configuration or a local module that it imports changes. Each occurrence is the result of one build: the files written, or the failure. A failed build does not end the subscription. Ending the subscription stops the watch; files already written stay.
